doc.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025

title: Starting clarinet at ten with a Benny Goodman tape
summary: His grandparents buy a pawn-shop clarinet and a Goodman cassette, and he knows immediately this is his life's work.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Did you have any memorable moments, epiphanies or aha! moments as a kid that set you on this path?

It was immediate. So — I began playing clarinet when I was ten years old in the fifth grade band. And I enjoyed swing music prior to that ‘cause I like old movies. I used to watch Abbott and Costello and I heard the Andrews Sisters and that music, so I kind of had a predisposition for that era already. And then fifth grade came along and you can join the band if you wanted to. And my grandfather just said to me, “I think you’d have fun with a clarinet.” Why he said that I don’t know. I think it was just divine intervention. But my grandparents bought me a clarinet at the local pawn shop, figuring it might give me a hobby. They didn’t know — nobody knew if I’d take to it or not. So they gave me the clarinet and at the same time they bought me a cassette tape of Benny Goodman just figuring that I’d get a kick out of this. And I don’t know how, but I just knew at that moment that this is what I want to do for the rest of my life. And I didn’t know if you

could or couldn’t. I didn’t know anything about the possibilities of a career failing or succeeding, I just knew that something really clicked. My life felt complete. And I learned a song by ear I think within the first week or two and I just moved my fingers around. I remember “I’ll be With You in Apple Blossom Time,” I just moved my fingers and I could play that melody. And so my teacher at the time, Jamie McLeod, who is a very dear friend of mine to this day, he was I think 26 and he played clarinet too, amazing clarinet player. And he got to meet Benny when Benny played at Hill Auditorium in Ann Arbor, Michigan, like a month or two before he passed away. So there was already that Goodman connection. And he was a great encouragement to me. So what I began doing was I’d play this cassette tape one microsecond at a time and try to play what I was hearing. And that’s pretty much how I learned most of my things was by ear you know. My reading has always lagged behind. But my ear, I could hear things and play them. So that’s how that early development came on. But yeah, I don’t know, I was very young but my life had meaning at that point.
